$comment: P45 lane td — [[D-CSUBSET-TYPEDEF-HEAD-DECORATION-TYPE-HIJACK]], the RUNNABLE half of the sweep. `resolveTypeNodeImpl` selects a type head FIRST-CHILD-THAT-RESOLVES-WINS and its token arm resolves ANY identifier through the scope chain as a possible type alias, so an identifier a decoration drags into a type-resolved child list can win over the real head and silently retype the declaration in a CLEAN-COMPILING program. Every typedef in main.c decorates its head with an attribute whose name (or whose second clause's name) is ALSO a live `typedef int` declared just above it — the collision that makes the hijack observable — across all four decoration slots (leading, after-keyword, mid, trailing) plus a two-clause form. ★ WHY THE EXIT CODE IS THE ASSERTION: the unit pins in tests/analysis/semantic/test_type_head_hijack_sweep.cpp stop at the resolved TypeId; this example carries the same answer through the real backend to an exit code, so a hijack surviving lowering changes the NUMBER. Truth rows are chosen so a wrong answer changes the exit: each hijacked `sizeof` reads 4 instead of 8 and drops 8 points, so a total hijack exits 2 rather than 42. ★★ `long long` vs `int` and NEVER `long` vs `int`: sizeof(long) is 8 under LP64 (linux/darwin) but 4 under LLP64 (windows pe64), so `long` would make the windows arm pass straight through the hijack it claims to guard; `long long` is 8 and `int` is 4 on all four targets here. ⚠ THE DECORATION IS `may_alias`/`unused`, NOT `aligned(16)`, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: DSS refuses `__attribute__((aligned(N)))` on a TYPEDEF with S_AlignasInvalidContext ('the alias resolves to the same type as its aliasee'), a separate pre-existing refusal carried by [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS-TYPEDEF-PARAM-PARSE]] (⚠ P58, 2026-09-03: that row is now CLOSED and NO LONGER GATED, so the '(gated;' this sentence used to carry is retired, and its clause number was wrong — the alignment specifier is C11 6.7.5p2 but C23 §6.7.6p2, C23's 6.7.5 being Function specifiers. The REFUSAL is unchanged and is the half this file leans on: an alignment specifier on a typedef is a constraint violation, and gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3, mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 AND MSVC 19.51 all refuse it, MEASURED 2026-09-03 each probed separately. P58 closed the row by making the ISO `typedef alignas(16) int T;` spelling draw the same S_AlignasInvalidContext instead of a bare parse error, and by ACCEPTING the specifier on a function PARAMETER, which this file does not use). MEASURED on this very file: with `aligned(16)` it does not COMPILE, so it would witness nothing. `may_alias`/`unused` have no layout sink, so the only question this file asks is the one it exists for. ⛔ THE TEMPTING WRONG FIX, recorded so it is never re-proposed: putting the attribute run INSIDE `typedefHeadFull`, 'where the type head already is' — it looks right and fails SILENTLY; the decoration belongs in a SIBLING slot (the row's `specifierPrefix`, the subtree `specifierPrefixChild` hands the alignas/noreturn/attribute scans). The REFUSAL half of this row — that wrong fix being rejected loudly by the ambiguous-head guard in `resolveTypeNodeImpl` — cannot be witnessed by a corpus example, because an example must BUILD; it lives in the unit suite as WrongFixInsideTheHeadIsRefusedLoudly, and the two must be read together. RED-ON-DISABLE for this file, MEASURED through the shipped CLI at x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec: apply the wrong fix to src/dss-config/sources/c.lang.json (move the attribute run out of `typedefDeclSpecifiers` into `typedefHeadFull`) — WITHOUT the ambiguous-head guard this example builds clean and exits 2 instead of 42 (every decorated `sizeof` reading 4); WITH the guard it fails to compile at all, error[S_InvalidTypeSpecifierCombination] 'ambiguous type head'. Either way it stops exiting 42. REFERENCE CONTROL, each probed SEPARATELY on THIS file at -std=c2x -Wall -Wextra: gcc 13.3.0 (WSL) and clang 18.1.3 (WSL) both build it with ZERO errors and ZERO warnings and both EXIT 42. On the same collision shape mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 also accepts and keeps the head type; MSVC 19.51 does not speak __attribute__, and its own __declspec(align(16)) spelling of the same question also keeps the head type. Three of four references accept, so under DSS = (gcc u clang u MSVC) u ISO C, DSS must accept it — and all four agree on what it MEANS.
